lines.trans: Quick check before three strikes: jacket buttoned, shoes polished—where are my glasses?!
Miracle of miracles, Mazen, they are sitting squarely on your nose!
Do not touch them! Table one has hot mint tea, black tea, and warm plates ready.
Suad is at the walnut piano, and both Room Two and Six guests are smiling!
We actually pulled off a six-hour celebration in a hundred and eighty minutes!
Listen—do you hear the municipal clock tower chiming three up Jasmine Street?
One chime, two chimes, three chimes... and wait, a car door just closed outside!
Someone just rang the brass gate bell twice—that is the signal from the brothers!
Look through the archway: Ziad is carrying a battered brown leather suitcase!
And walking beside Rami with a silver walking stick and a wide straw hat...
Remember to lift the iron gate handle slightly first, Mazen, and smile!
Welcome back to Jasmine Courtyard House, my friend—thirty summers to the very week!

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: Form IV verb meaning to complete a task cleanly or deliver on time.

examples.trans: We got all the orders done before sunset.

examples.text: بتنجزي الشغل أسرع لما تشتغلي بهدوء.
examples.trans: You finish the work faster when you work calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used for traffic lights, hand gestures, and railway or stage signals.

examples.text: وقفنا عند أول إشارة بعد المحطة.
examples.trans: We stopped at the first traffic light after the station.

examples.text: اعطيني إشارة بإيدك بس يبدأ العزف.
examples.trans: Give me a hand signal as soon as the playing starts.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

اتسكّر.gloss: to close; shut; get locked up

meanings.en: to close; shut; get locked up
meanings.note: Form V passive/reflexive of سكّر in spoken Jordanian Arabic: to close up on its own or be closed for the day.

examples.trans: The door shut from the strong wind.
The bakery closes at ten at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بالضبط.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بالضبط.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أبراج.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Colloquial Form II verbal noun coined from Arabicized شيّك ('to check', from English). Used for quick safety or list checks.

examples.text: نعمل تشييك سريع عالأغراض قبل ما نطلع.
examples.trans: Let's do a quick check on the things before we head out.

examples.text: تشييك الكهربا أخد خمس دقايق بس.
examples.trans: The electrical check took only five minutes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جلود.

examples.trans: This is a small brown leather notebook.
The leather bag is heavy and sturdy.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حفلات.

examples.trans: He designs concert halls.
We attended a lovely music concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدق, بيدق).

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Active participle of سمع ('to hear'), standard in Jordanian for 'can you hear?' (سامعني؟).

examples.trans: I hear you clearly on the phone.
Do you hear the sound of a car outside the gate?

meanings.note: Numeral 'six'; short form ست (sitt) before a plural noun (ست سنين 'six years').

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سيارات.

examples.trans: We heard a car stop outside.

examples.text: ما في صوت سيارات جوا الساحة.
examples.trans: There is no sound of cars inside the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine صديقة, broken plural أصدقاء).

examples.trans: This is my friend from university days.
All our friends gathered at the party.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عريضة, plural: عراض).

examples.trans: The wide desk under the window is comfortable.
There are wide wooden beams in the ceiling.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (also feminine عكازة) used for a hiker's walking stick or a crutch.

examples.trans: My grandfather walks with an old wooden walking stick.
A hiking stick helps on the steep climb.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Verbal noun from عاد ('to return'), used in phrases like حمد لله عالعودة or بعودتك.

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بعودتك بالسلامة يا طارق.
examples.trans: We were very happy at your safe return, Tariq.

examples.text: تذكرة الذهاب والعودة أوفر من المفرد.
examples.trans: A round-trip ticket is cheaper than a single.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فضية, plural: فضيين).

examples.trans: Here is the small silver key to the attic.
An old silver tea tray.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative from فعل ('deed'), used to confirm a surprising or welcome fact.

examples.text: فعلا الجو برد كتير بعد المغرب.
examples.trans: Actually, the weather got very cold after sunset.
This work really turned out well crafted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاعدة, plural: قاعدين).

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a brimmed sun hat, straw hat, or cap.

examples.text: البس قبعة قش لما تمشي بالشمس.
examples.trans: Wear a straw hat when you walk in the sun.
Her floral hat is hanging on the door.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for woven straw used in hats, baskets, and matting.

examples.trans: We bought a straw basket for fresh bread.
A straw hat is light and comfortable in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماشية, plural: ماشيين).

examples.trans: I saw my brother walking down this street.
Everything is going smoothly.

meanings.note: Active participle of ابتسم ('to smile').

examples.text: أبو طارق وقف بنص الساحة مبتسم ومبسوط.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq stood in the middle of the courtyard smiling happily.

examples.text: نور بتستقبل الضيوف الصبح بوجه بشوش ومبتسم.
examples.trans: Nour greets guests in the morning with a warm, smiling face.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مسكرة, plural: مسكرين).

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
The main water valve is shut off now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.text: الشارع على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The street is five minutes away on foot.
Walking in the morning in Amman is enjoyable.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Feminine noun from عجز ('to be unable'), meaning an extraordinary feat or lucky miracle.

examples.text: إننا خلصنا كل شي بوقت قياسي هاد معجزة!
examples.trans: That we finished everything in record time is a miracle!

examples.text: أبو سعاد بيعمل معجزات بالمطبخ الصغير.
examples.trans: Suad's father works wonders in the small kitchen.

meanings.note: Passive participle of لمّع ('to polish shoes, brass, or wood').

examples.text: مازن إجا بقميص أبيض مكوي وحذاء أسود ملمع.
examples.trans: Mazen arrived in a pressed white shirt and polished black shoes.

examples.text: الطاولات الخشب الملمعة بتعكس ضو الفوانيس.
examples.trans: The polished wooden tables reflect the glow of the lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.
